phases.title: Foundations
phases.description: Build accounting literacy — read a P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statement, and trace how money moves through a business.

phases.title: Markets & Instruments
phases.description: Understand the instruments (equity, debt, derivatives) and the players — how sell-side and buy-side firms differ.

phases.title: Corporate Finance
phases.description: Learn how firms fund themselves and choose investments — capital structure, WACC, capital budgeting, working capital.

phases.title: Equity Research & Valuation
phases.description: Go deep on the analyst's toolkit — build a DCF from discount-rate first principles, run a rigorous comps screen, and use precedent transactions and trading multiples to triangulate an enterprise value.

phases.title: Advanced Financial Modeling
phases.description: Go beyond reading statements — build a fully integrated 3-statement model from scratch, layer in acquisition debt with an LBO model, and analyze credit risk the way a lender does.

phases.title: Investment Banking & M&A
phases.description: Learn how deals are structured and value is created or destroyed — synergies, due diligence, post-merger integration.

phases.title: Private Equity & Alternative Investments
phases.description: Explore the buy-side beyond public markets — how private equity funds source and structure deals, how hedge funds generate returns across strategies, and how venture capital evaluates early-stage bets.

phases.title: Leveraged Finance, Credit & Restructuring
phases.description: The debt side of the deal, and what happens when it goes wrong: the leveraged product set, how credit agreements actually constrain a borrower, and the in- and out-of-court routes through distress.

phases.title: Private Credit, Distressed & Special Situations
phases.description: Buying and holding debt rather than advising on it: bilateral lending that never gets syndicated, and investing in claims on companies in trouble.

phases.title: Structured Finance & Derivatives
phases.description: Understand how assets are pooled and tranched into securities, how options and Greeks govern hedging decisions, and how interest-rate and credit derivatives reshape risk across a portfolio.

phases.title: Specialised Coverage & Asset-Class Modelling
phases.description: Where the standard model breaks. A bank has no EBITDA and no free cash flow; a building is priced on NOI and a cap rate; a toll road is a debt-sizing exercise with no terminal value. Each needs its own mental model.

phases.title: Forensic Financial Analysis
phases.description: Look past the headline numbers — detect earnings manipulation through accruals analysis, identify off-balance-sheet exposure hidden in SPVs, and spot the red flags that preceded the biggest accounting scandals.

phases.title: Applied
phases.description: Apply it all to real filings and mock deals — read 10-Ks/10-Qs, practice deal exercises, prep for finance interviews.

topics.title: Reading the Three Statements
topics.description: Learn what each of the three statements reports and how they lock together: net income flows to retained earnings, and the cash flow statement reconciles accrual profit back to cash. The literacy everything later assumes.

steps.d: Say what each statement measures and over what period.
Follow a sale from revenue through receivables to cash collected.
Start from net income and rebuild the cash flow statement's operating section.

topics.title: Accounting Fundamentals
topics.description: Understand the accrual mechanics behind the numbers — revenue recognition, matching, depreciation, deferred taxes, working capital — and where management judgement enters. This is what separates reading a statement from trusting it.

steps.d: Work an example where the two diverge and explain why.
Book revenue recognition, prepaid expenses and depreciation by hand.
Pick a filing and list three policy choices management could have made differently.

topics.title: Time Value of Money & Discounting
topics.description: Money today is worth more than money later, and every valuation in this course rests on that. Present and future value, compounding, annuities and perpetuities, and the discount rate as the price of waiting.

steps.d: Grow a sum at a rate over n periods and see the curve bend.
Bring a future cash flow to today, then flex the rate and watch the value move.
Price an annuity and a perpetuity from first principles.
Discount a three-year forecast by hand — this is a DCF in miniature.

topics.title: Instruments: Equities, Debt & Derivatives
topics.description: Work through the three instrument families — equity, debt, derivatives — and what each one is a claim on, how it is issued, and what drives its price.

steps.d: Place equity, debt and derivatives on a seniority and payoff map.
Track a share and a bond from issuer to investor.
Name the two or three variables that move each instrument most.

topics.title: The Industry Map: Buy-Side vs Sell-Side
topics.description: Map the industry: who manages capital and who intermediates it, how banks, asset managers, hedge funds and research desks make money, and which seat does which work.

steps.d: List who raises capital, who allocates it, and who advises.
Trace one order from a buy-side PM through a sell-side desk.
Write what a day looks like in two roles you might actually want.

topics.title: Risk, Return & Portfolio Construction
topics.description: Risk and return as a pair: diversification, correlation, beta and the risk-free rate, then how asset allocation turns them into a portfolio. These primitives feed the cost of equity in the next phase.

steps.d: Compute volatility and correlation for two assets and combine them.
Build a two- and then five-asset portfolio and watch risk fall faster than return.
Write a policy mix for one stated objective and defend the weights.

topics.title: The Map of Finance: Coverage vs Product Groups
topics.description: Where the seats actually are inside a bank: industry coverage versus product groups (M&A, leveraged finance, ECM/DCM, restructuring), and the financial sponsors desk that sits between the bank and private equity.

steps.d: Work out who originates a deal and who executes it.
Take one announced transaction and name every group that touched it.
Why FSG is the strongest feeder into private equity.
Choose two groups you would actually recruit for and justify it.

topics.title: Cost of Capital & WACC
topics.description: Build a discount rate from its parts: cost of equity via CAPM, after-tax cost of debt, and the market-value weights between them. You learn the formula here; the valuation phase stress-tests it inside a live DCF.

steps.d: Assemble CAPM from risk-free rate, beta and equity risk premium.
Get to an after-tax cost of debt and justify the tax shield.
Combine at market values, then flex beta and see WACC move.

topics.title: Capital Structure & Capital Budgeting
topics.description: How a firm decides what to fund and how to fund it: NPV and IRR project selection, the debt-versus-equity trade-off, and working capital policy.

steps.d: Compute NPV and IRR on the same cash flows and explain where they disagree.
Argue debt versus equity for one firm on cost, flexibility and risk.
Build a cash conversion cycle and say what shortening it is worth.

topics.title: DCF Deep Dive
topics.description: Go beyond a basic DCF — build a rigorous WACC from scratch, stress-test terminal value assumptions with sensitivity tables, and understand why terminal value typically drives 60–80% of valuation output.

steps.d: Build unlevered FCF off the operating model.
Rebuild WACC for this company, not a textbook one.
Compute it both ways and show what share of value it carries.
Run a WACC-versus-growth grid and state the range you would defend.

topics.title: Comparable Company Analysis (Comps)
topics.description: Screen and select a peer group, calculate EV/EBITDA, P/E, and EV/Revenue multiples consistently across companies, and build a football-field valuation range.

steps.d: Pick a comp set and write the criteria that admitted each one.
Put everyone on the same fiscal basis and use LTM or NTM consistently.
Compute EV/EBITDA, P/E and EV/Revenue, then benchmark on median not mean.

topics.title: Precedent Transactions & Control Premiums
topics.description: Distinguish trading comps (current market prices) from deal comps (acquisition premiums baked in), and use precedent transactions to anchor the control premium in a negotiated sale.

steps.d: Build a precedent set filtered on sector, size and vintage.
Back out the control premium implied by each transaction.
Explain why deal comps sit above trading comps and when they shouldn't.

topics.title: 3-Statement Modeling
topics.description: Build a fully linked income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement in Excel from scratch — the foundational build behind every advanced model, versus just reading one.

steps.d: Build an assumptions block and forecast the income statement off it.
Link the cash flow statement so the balance sheet balances with no plug.
Change one driver and find every cell that should have moved.

topics.title: Credit Analysis & Debt Schedules
topics.description: Analyze a borrower the way a lender does — leverage and coverage ratios, covenant headroom — and build a debt schedule with interest, amortization, and cash sweep mechanics.

steps.d: Compute leverage, interest coverage and fixed-charge coverage on a real borrower.
Find headroom and the EBITDA decline that breaches.
Model each tranche with interest, amortisation and sweep, circularity handled.

topics.title: LBO Modeling
topics.description: Model a leveraged buyout end to end: sources & uses, acquisition debt tranches, cash sweeps, and the return math (IRR/MOIC) private equity firms underwrite deals on.

steps.d: Fund a purchase price and reconcile to the entry equity cheque.
Tranche the capital structure and run interest and mandatory amortisation.
Pay down with free cash flow, then exit and solve IRR and MOIC.
Flex entry multiple, leverage and exit multiple in a returns grid.

topics.title: The M&A Deal Process & Due Diligence
topics.description: The deal from mandate to close: buyer outreach, LOI, confirmatory diligence and signing, plus what diligence actually interrogates across financial, legal and commercial workstreams.

steps.d: Lay out mandate, marketing, LOI, diligence, signing and close with who drives each.
Pull a checklist and mark the ten items that would kill a deal.
Pick a collapsed deal and identify where in the process it failed.

topics.title: Sell-Side Process: Teaser, NDA & CIM
topics.description: What bankers actually produce between mandate and close, and how a buyer reads it: the anonymous teaser, the NDA, the CIM, the process letter and the buyer list.

steps.d: Teaser to NDA to CIM to bids — what each document is for and who sees it.
Read a real one and note what it asserts, what it omits, and why it never states a price.
Segment strategics vs sponsors for a target and justify the cut.

topics.title: Pitch Books
topics.description: What a pitch book is for and how it is assembled — situation overview, market update, valuation football field, and the recommendation the whole deck exists to support.

steps.d: Dissect a published pitch book and name what each section is doing.
Assemble a valuation range from DCF, comps and precedents.
Draft the recommendation page and make every prior slide support it.

topics.title: Merger Models & Accretion/Dilution
topics.description: Build a pro-forma EPS bridge: consideration mix, synergies, foregone interest and the break-even premium. The most-tested technical in an IB interview.

steps.d: Combine the two P&Ls, layer in the financing, and get to pro-forma EPS.
Solve for the premium at which the deal stops being accretive.
Rerun it as all-cash, all-stock and mixed; explain why the answer moves.

topics.title: Synergies & Post-Merger Integration
topics.description: Where the premium is supposed to come back from: cost and revenue synergies, how each is quantified and phased, and why integration is where most of the value is lost.

steps.d: Separate cost from revenue and say which one underwriters believe.
Put a number and a realisation timeline on three specific synergies.
Subtract integration costs and restate the premium the deal can bear.

topics.title: Equity & Debt Capital Markets
topics.description: How companies actually raise money: the IPO process end to end, follow-ons and convertibles on the equity side, investment-grade issuance on the debt side, and how ECM and DCM desks differ from M&A.

steps.d: Underwriter selection, S-1, roadshow, bookbuilding, pricing and the first day.
Pull one from EDGAR and find the risk factors, use of proceeds and dilution.
ECM vs DCM vs LevFin — who does what, and what the work looks like day to day.

topics.title: Private Equity Fundamentals
topics.description: How PE funds are structured (GP/LP, fees, carry), how they source and screen deals, and how a buyout thesis turns into an investment.

steps.d: GP versus LP, management fee, carry and the fund lifecycle.
Apply a buyout screen to a real company and pass or kill it.
State the entry case, the value-creation plan and the exit in one page.

topics.title: Fund Economics & Value Creation
topics.description: How a fund actually makes money and how returns get attributed: hurdle, catch-up, European vs American waterfall, and splitting an outcome into deleveraging, EBITDA growth and multiple expansion.

steps.d: Run an exit through European and American structures and compare GP take.
Decompose an IRR into deleveraging, earnings growth and multiple arbitrage.
Decide which lever did the work — and whether it was skill or the market.

topics.title: Hedge Fund Strategies
topics.description: Survey the core hedge fund strategies — long/short equity, global macro, quant, event-driven, arbitrage — and how each generates returns.

steps.d: Define long/short, macro, quant, event-driven and arbitrage by return source.
Name what each one is really exposed to.
Write a thesis, the catalyst and how you would size it.

topics.title: Venture Capital Basics
topics.description: How VC funds are structured and how they evaluate, price, and structure early-stage investments — from thesis to term sheet.

steps.d: Seed through Series C — who invests, what changes each time.
Work pre- and post-money, option pool and the founder dilution.
Find liquidation preference, participation and anti-dilution and say who they protect.

topics.title: Growth Equity & Secondaries
topics.description: The two private-equity adjacencies with their own recruiting tracks: growth equity's minority, low-leverage case study, and the secondaries market's pricing at a discount to NAV.

steps.d: Work cohort retention and unit economics on a real-shaped business.
Value it without leverage — the LBO maths does not apply.
Value an LP position at a discount to NAV and justify the discount.
Follow a GP-led secondary from motive to close.

topics.title: Leveraged Loans & High Yield
topics.description: The leveraged product set: term loan B versus senior notes, pricing and call protection, and the CLO and high-yield-fund buyer base that decides what can actually get financed.

steps.d: Term loan B vs senior notes: security, seniority, floating vs fixed, call protection.
Work out who buys each — CLOs, HY funds, direct lenders — and how that shapes terms.
Take a recent LBO and reason through why its capital structure was built the way it was.

topics.title: Restructuring & Chapter 11
topics.description: In-court versus out-of-court, creditor hierarchy and the absolute priority rule, DIP financing, liquidation analysis and the plan of reorganisation — plus how restructuring interviews differ from standard IB.

steps.d: Absolute priority rule: who gets paid, in what order, and where the fulcrum security sits.
Out-of-court exchange vs Chapter 11 — the trade-offs on speed, cost and holdouts.
Recovery by class, and what it implies for where value breaks.
Work the RX interview question set until the answers are yours.

topics.title: Private Credit & Direct Lending
topics.description: Non-bank lenders underwrite bilaterally and hold to maturity, so documentation and downside protection matter more than syndication flex. The fastest-growing seat in the market.

steps.d: Direct lending versus broadly syndicated leveraged finance.
Roll first and second lien into one tranche and price the all-in yield.
Model a case that trips a covenant and see what the lender can do.
Understand the BDC and fund structures behind the money.

topics.title: Distressed Debt & Event-Driven Investing
topics.description: Buying claims rather than advising on them. Find the fulcrum security, value the estate, and take a view on recovery or control — a different discipline from the restructuring advisory taught earlier.

steps.d: Locate the security that converts to equity in a reorganisation.
Price the claim, not the company — at a price, with a recovery view.
Run a recovery waterfall and the path to control.
Frame a catalyst and size a merger-arbitrage position.

topics.title: Options & Greeks Fundamentals
topics.description: How call and put options are priced, how payoff diagrams work, and how the Greeks — delta, gamma, theta, vega — measure each dimension of an option position's risk.

steps.d: Diagram long and short calls and puts at expiry.
Separate intrinsic from time value and see what moves each.
Show how delta, gamma, theta and vega each change a position's P&L.
Delta-hedge a position and explain why it needs re-hedging.

topics.title: Interest Rate & Credit Derivatives
topics.description: How interest rate swaps transfer rate risk between counterparties, and how credit default swaps transfer credit risk — the instruments at the heart of fixed-income and credit risk management.

steps.d: Build a fixed-for-floating swap and identify each leg's exposure.
Explain why a corporate borrower would enter one.
Price a CDS as insurance and define exactly what triggers a credit event.

topics.title: Securitization & ABS/MBS Basics
topics.description: How loans are pooled and tranched into asset-backed securities — the mechanics of cash-flow waterfalls, credit enhancement, and the key differences between ABS and MBS.

steps.d: Take a loan pool and cut it into senior, mezzanine and equity.
Allocate cash and losses through the stack in order.
Apply overcollateralisation and excess spread, then compare ABS to MBS.

topics.title: Risk, Capital & ALM
topics.description: The risk seat's own vocabulary: value at risk for market risk, risk-weighted assets and CET1 for capital, CVA for counterparty exposure, and EVE and NII for the banking book.

steps.d: Calculate it, then say plainly what it does not tell you.
Find RWA and CET1 in a real bank disclosure.
Understand CVA and why Basel III charged for it.
Work economic value of equity and net interest income sensitivity.

topics.title: FIG: Modelling Banks & Insurers
topics.description: Banks have no EBITDA and no free cash flow. You model the balance sheet first, drive earnings off net interest margin and provisions, and value on price-to-tangible-book and a dividend discount model.

steps.d: Start with assets and funding, not revenue.
Model net interest margin, provisions and regulatory capital.
Use P/TBV and DDM — EV/EBITDA is meaningless here.
Work tangible book dilution and the earn-back period.

topics.title: Real Estate Finance & REITs
topics.description: Property is valued on net operating income and a cap rate, not an EBITDA multiple. REITs report FFO and AFFO instead of EPS and trade at a premium or discount to net asset value.

steps.d: Build NOI, apply a cap rate, and get to an exit value.
Assemble a REIT net asset value and compare it to the share price.
Tie FFO, AFFO and CAD back to net income.
Work a JV equity promote between sponsor and investor.

topics.title: Project & Infrastructure Finance
topics.description: Non-recourse, single-asset financing sized off contracted cash flows. The model is a debt-sizing exercise around DSCR and LLCR inside an SPV, with no terminal value anywhere in it.

steps.d: Construct cash flow available for debt service for one asset.
Size and shape repayment to a target DSCR.
Work LLCR and the lender protections around it.
Say why corporate finance intuitions fail on a project.

topics.title: Earnings Quality & Accruals Analysis
topics.description: Assess whether reported earnings reflect real cash generation or aggressive accrual-accounting choices — the foundation of any forensic analysis.

steps.d: Put net income next to cash from operations over five years.
Compute the accrual ratio and flag the years it spikes.
Tie a spike to a specific policy or one-off and judge whether earnings are real.

topics.title: Off-Balance-Sheet Items & SPVs
topics.description: Identify leverage and commitments that do not appear on the balance sheet — operating leases, SPVs, synthetic securitizations — and understand when accounting standards require consolidation.

steps.d: Find commitments, guarantees and leases disclosed but not on the face.
Work out what it holds, who bears the risk, and whether it consolidates.
Add the off-balance-sheet items back and recompute the ratios.

topics.title: Red Flags in Financial Statements
topics.description: The warning signs that preceded Enron, WorldCom, and the 2008 crisis — rapidly growing receivables, channel stuffing, related-party transactions, and the Beneish M-Score manipulation detector.

steps.d: Receivables and inventory growing ahead of revenue, margin outliers, related parties.
Run a Beneish M-Score on one company and interpret the output.
Take Enron or WorldCom and mark which flags were visible in the last clean filing.

topics.title: Reading 10-Ks & 10-Qs
topics.description: Navigate a real 10-K and 10-Q section by section — MD&A, risk factors, the footnotes and the segment data — and pull the numbers a model actually needs out of a filing.

steps.d: Items 1, 1A, 7 and 8 — what each is for and what it hides.
Extract debt terms, leases, segments and share count.
Pull a filing into a driver sheet and reconcile every input to a page number.

topics.title: Deal Practice & Interview Prep
topics.description: Rehearse under deal conditions: paper LBOs, timed modelling tests, and the technical question set, until the reasoning is fast enough to survive an interview.

steps.d: Approximate IRR and MOIC with no spreadsheet, under time.
Run the timed LBO test, then diff your build against the solution.
Work the DCF, comps and accretion/dilution question sets until answers are yours.
Run one full interview out loud with someone else scoring.

topics.title: Indian Capital Markets, SEBI & Career Paths
topics.description: The regulatory and market architecture an analyst in India is actually asked about, plus an honest read on CFA versus CA versus FRM and where the Indian deal market hires.

steps.d: SEBI, NSE and BSE, the depositories and clearing corporations.
DRHP, book-building and the anchor book.
Indian investment banking and private equity, and who hires in Mumbai.
Pick between CFA, CA and FRM for the seat you actually want.
